text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Four persons were killed on Friday in Onitsha, eastern Nigeria, in bomb blasts in two different parts of the city.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha, in a message to an army function, says Nigeria will do business with only countries that respect its sovereignty and relate to it on equal basis.
- Government lawyers on Friday opposed an application for bail by 19 youths from the Ogoni tribe held since a 1994 murder of four Ogoni chiefs.
- A Lagos high court defers till next Wednesday ruling on bail application by dissidents charged with treason over the recent spate of bomb explosions in Nigeria.
- The federal government on Friday banned British Airways from flying to Nigeria, the airline's second most profitable route after New York.
- Statistics from the Nigeria Employers Consultative Association show that despite macro-economic stability in the 18 months to December 31, 1996 there was a 10 percent decline in employment.
